rich_summary: Sita, alone in the forest while Rama and Lakshmana are away, receives a visitor disguised as a mendicant—Ravana, who has come intending to abduct her. Bound by duty to treat a supposed brahmin with respect, she introduces herself and recounts the story of Rama’s exile: Kaikeyi’s demand, Dasaratha’s reluctant obedience, and Rama’s steadfast acceptance of banishment. Ravana then drops his disguise in words, declaring himself the feared king of the titans and tempting Sita with wealth and queenship in Lanka. Sita responds with fierce devotion and scorn, praising Rama’s greatness while mocking Ravana’s arrogance through vivid comparisons. The exchange heightens the tension before the impending abduction, revealing Sita’s moral courage and unwavering loyalty in the face of intimidation.

highlight_spans.why: Sita’s courteous response to the disguised Ravana shows her adherence to dharma—respecting a supposed brahmin guest even while vulnerable.
Sita recounts Rama’s exile and loyalty to his father’s command, a pivotal recap that frames the moral stakes of the coming conflict.
Sita’s furious rebuke comparing Ravana to a jackal desiring a lioness captures her fearless devotion and the emotional peak of the confrontation.

top_scenes.scene_text: Ravana disguised as a mendicant stands before Sita in the forest hermitage while she respectfully addresses him, unaware of the danger.
Ravana reveals his identity to Sita in the lonely forest clearing, boasting of his power and the golden city of Lanka across the sea.
Sita, trembling yet defiant, rebukes Ravana with fierce words, comparing him to a jackal before a lion while the dark forest surrounds them.
